record.original_question: Hentgartner and Schobe [432] and Goodman and Saff [344] have shown that if f (z) = z + a2 z 2 + . . . maps D univalently onto a domain G1 that is convex in the direction of the imaginary axis (CIA), then Gr = {f (|z| < r)} is not necessarily CIA for all r, r < 1, or even for r bigger than some constant. (a) Find sup{r :√Gr is necessarily CIA}. (A result of Goodman and Saff [344] suggests that this is 2 − 1.) (b) Find reasonable sufficient conditions on G1 (or, equivalently, on f ) that imply that Gr is in CIA for all r in (0, 1). (c) Suppose that we slit G1 along the real axis and let G′ , G′′ be those two components of the resulting family of domains that have 0 on their boundaries. If G1 = G′ ∪G′′ , does it necessarily follow that Gr is CIA for all r in (0, 1)? (d) If G1 is CIA but Gr0 is not CIA, is it true that Gr is not CIA for r0 < r < 1? (D. A. Brannan)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let f be analytic and univalent in the open unit disk D = {z ∈ ℂ : |z| < 1}, with Taylor expansion f(z) = z + a₂z² + a₃z³ + ⋯, and let G₁ = f(D). For 0 < r < 1, set G_r = f({z : |z| < r}). A domain G ⊂ ℂ is said to be convex in the direction of the imaginary axis (CIA) if, for every c ∈ ℂ, the intersection of G with the vertical line {z : Re z = Re c} is either empty or a (possibly unbounded) connected segment.

Suppose throughout that G₁ is CIA.

(a) Determine sup{r ∈ (0,1) : for every f as above with G₁ CIA, the domain G_r is necessarily CIA}.

(b) Find natural sufficient conditions on G₁ (equivalently on f) under which G_r is CIA for every r ∈ (0,1).

(c) Slit G₁ along the real axis and let G′, G″ denote the two components of the resulting (possibly disconnected) open set that contain 0 on their boundaries. Assume that G₁ = G′ ∪ G″ ∪ (G₁ ∩ ℝ). Does it follow that G_r is CIA for every r ∈ (0,1)?

(d) If G₁ is CIA but there exists r₀ ∈ (0,1) such that G_{r₀} fails to be CIA, must G_r fail to be CIA for every r ∈ (r₀, 1)?
artifact.status_search_result: Part (a) was settled by Ruscheweyh and Salinas (Ann. Acad. Sci. Fenn., 1989), who proved that the supremum equals √2 − 1, confirming the Goodman–Saff conjecture: for 0 < r ≤ √2 − 1, f(rz) preserves convexity in any given direction whenever f does, and this fails for any larger r. Parts (b), (c) and (d) do not appear to have widely known definitive resolutions in the available literature, so the problem as a whole is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: On the preservation of direction-convexity and the Goodman-Saff conjecture (Ruscheweyh, Salinas)
status_evidence.snippet: Ruscheweyh and Salinas showed that the condition is satisfied for 0 < r ≤ √2 − 1, and for no larger value of r, which settled the Goodman-Saff conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Part (a) is solved: the radius equals √2 − 1.

status_evidence.title: On the Preservation of Direction Convexity under Differentiation and Integration
status_evidence.snippet: Subsequent work by Ruscheweyh and others on direction-convexity preservation under various operations.
status_evidence.claim: The DCP-radius problem of Goodman–Saff has been studied and resolved for the dilation operator with bound √2−1.
